original.target_description: Study 1, fairness judgment of own selfish task allocation (Condition 1) versus an unaffiliated other committing the same action (Condition 2), excluding altruistic/randomizer choices. Figure 1 reports bounds for comparisons between starred and unstarred bars, including this comparison.

n.sample_role: Participants in Conditions 1 and 2; target comparison analytic sample size not separately printed.
n.exclusions: Two Condition 1 subjects excluded for altruistic behavior or randomizer use. Total recruited across all four conditions was 76; this is not the target pair analytic n.
n.location: p. 690 (PDF p. 2), Results and Discussion; p. 689, Method
n.quote: Two subjects in Condition 1 were removed from analysis

es.location: p. 690 (PDF p. 2), Figure 1 caption and Results and Discussion

p.location: p. 690 (PDF p. 2), Figure 1 caption, starred versus unstarred bars (self versus other included)

replication.target_description: Experiment 1, minimal groups, preregistered extension Hypothesis 2: own fairness versus others after the same transgression, altruists excluded. Planned contrast uses self weight 3 versus other, in-group, out-group weights -1 each. This is self versus all other conditions, rather than only the unaffiliated-other pair.

n.sample_role: Participants in Experiment 1 four-condition planned contrast after exclusions; exact analytic n cannot be established unambiguously from printed counts.
n.exclusions: Results report 610 recruited, 6 attention-check failures, 9 duplicates, 5 nonconsents, and final sample 590 before removing 47 randomizer users and 4 altruists. Contrast denominator df is 536; neighboring power paragraph calls 536 final sample size. These counts are internally inconsistent.
n.location: pp. 805–806 (PDF pp. 8–9), Experiment 1 Results and preregistered replication analyses
n.quote: our final sample consisted of 590 participants

es.location: p. 806 (PDF p. 9), Preregistered extension analyses, first paragraph

p.location: p. 806 (PDF p. 9), Preregistered extension analyses, first paragraph

reported_success.location: p. 811 (PDF p. 14), discussion of individual moral hypocrisy
reported_success.quote: When only transgressors were included in our sample, we did not find that participants rated themselves as more moral than others.

notes: Titles verified against supplied references. Original Figure 1 provides only a shared t/p bound for the targeted self–other comparison; no effect size was printed for that pair. Original d = 1.11 and p = .001 belong to a different contrast (self plus in-group versus unaffiliated other plus out-group) and were not substituted. Replication p. 9 points to Experiment 1; the self-versus-all-others extension excluding altruists is extracted, not the intergroup main contrast or the intent-to-treat version. Analytic n left null on both sides rather than deriving it or substituting total enrollment or inconsistent power-analysis counts.
